entities.summary: King Hoel, also known as Sir Howel, Saint Hywel and Hywel the Great, was a late 5th- and early 6th-century member of the ruling dynasty of Cornouaille. He may have ruled Cornouaille jointly after the restoration of his father, Budic II of Brittany, but he seems to have predeceased his father and left his young son, Tewdwr, as Budic's heir. Hoel's reign marked a significant turning point in the history of Brittany, as he successfully defended the region against the Frankish invasions and established a strong foundation for the future growth of Brittany. His military campaigns and diplomatic efforts also had a lasting impact on the region's relations with its neighbors, including the Franks and the Visigoths. The legacy of King Hoel can be seen in the continued cultural and linguistic ties between Brittany and its Celtic heritage. As the founder of the dynasty that ruled Cornouaille, Hoel's influence extended beyond his own lifetime, shaping the course of Breton history for centuries to come. Despite the lack of definitive records, Hoel's reputation as a wise and just ruler has endured, with many historians and scholars continuing to study and debate his life and reign.
